summary.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was Rs 1,930 crore with EBITDA of Rs 199 crore (10.32% margin, up from 10.11%), and standalone PBT rose about 26% YoY to Rs 72 crore. Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Completed three HAM packages worth Rs 1,700 crore on Bengaluru-Vijayawada Expressway (AP), all ahead of COD. Management says revenue from large new projects (transmission, roads, solar, water) has not yet started and will ramp from Q2-Q3.

segments.name: MDO (Mining)
segments.commentary: Q1 coal production 4.79 MT; MDO revenue about Rs 362 crore in the quarter per analyst calculation. Siarmal planned 27 MT and Pachhwara 7 MT for FY27; FY29 target 57 MT retained. Pottangi Bauxite production not yet started.

segments.name: Multi-asset platform (InvIT/HAM)
segments.commentary: Holds units worth about Rs 1,521 crore (Rs 1,314 crore Anantam Highway Trust plus Rs 207 crore Shrem InvIT). Next tranche of 11 HAM assets to be transferred to Anantam InvIT by March 2027, expected to yield about Rs 1,700-1,800 crore of units for <Rs 81 crore incremental equity.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 10-12% (reconfirmed; analyst noted 11-12%).
Revenue growth guidance of 30-40% for FY27 reiterated; ramp-up expected from Q3, stronger in Q4 and into Q1 FY28.
Standalone debt reduction guidance of Rs 600-800 crore for FY27 reiterated; standalone net-debt-positive target by FY28 reaffirmed.
FY27 order inflow guidance of Rs 10,000-12,000 crore reiterated; bids worth Rs 15,000-20,000 crore pending opening.
Working capital days expected to reach about 120 by year-end and about 90 next year; from 131-133 days currently.
Finance cost for FY27 targeted at about Rs 350 crore.
Standalone capex guided at under Rs 100 crore for FY27, unchanged.
Coal production target of 57 MT by FY29; coal handling plant (CHP) expected to take about 1.5 years, with Siarmal at 27 MT (FY27), 35 MT (FY28), 50 MT after CHP.
capex_capacity: Siarmal total original capex Rs 2,730 crore, about 40-45% spent; more than 50% of equity already invested; around Rs 300 crore cash sitting at Siarmal SPV; Rs 235 crore residual equity to be funded from SPV accruals.
Siarmal debt sanction Rs 2,000 crore, Rs 60 crore drawn as of 30 June; around Rs 300 crore remaining to draw.

Transmission and solar stake sale to Alpha Alternatives: total equity requirement about Rs 1,600-1,650 crore; Alpha to co-invest 49% during construction; about Rs 900 crore structured equity already raised.

Anantam InvIT: 11 HAM assets, 4 to be flipped in August; 4 CODs done and 3 more by September; all 18 assets targeted for transfer by FY27 end or Q1 FY28, subject to NHAI NOC after six months of first annuity.
Other pipeline: 1977 MW solar mandate, Mekhali interstate transmission (Karnataka), water HAM, oil and gas portfolio to be considered for a future InvIT structure.
demand_pricing: NHAI FY27 pipeline: 54 highway/expressway projects, 2,442 km, about Rs 1.80 lakh crore (26 EPC, 21 HAM, 7 BOT). Awarding in Q1 was soft, particularly in national highways.
NHAI monetisation: 17 stretches (~1,693 km) targeted for FY27 via TOT/InvIT, expected proceeds Rs 30,000-35,000 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 1.5 lakh crore per Rohan; management later cited Rs 2.5-3 lakh crore across sectors, of which roads about Rs 1.25 lakh crore.
Declared L1 for Sikasar to Kodar Reservoir Link Canal Pipeline (Chhattisgarh), lump sum about Rs 2,524 crore.
Mining balance contract value about Rs 1.03 lakh crore; MDO reported order book about Rs 5,224 crore (3-year rolling).
Coal MDO pricing: Siarmal about Rs 550-600/t; Pachhwara about Rs 1,150-1,200/t; Siarmal coal fee currently 78%, moving to 100% after CHP.
Input costs: diesel bought at about Rs 140 and bitumen prices roughly doubled during the recent disruption; government reimburses 60-65% of fuel and bitumen cost increase.
